minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 10, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:01 p.m., on May 10, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 6, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum (arrived at 5:04 p.m.)
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel and Cyber Security Operations Manager Pursuant to
  Government Code 54957(a) on Matters Posing a Threat to Public Services, Facilities
  and Operations; City of Mission Viejo.

City Council Minutes  1  May 10, 2016
 RECESS

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was nothing to report from Closed Session.

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Musical Performance by the La Paz Jazz Combo of La Paz Intermediate School

  Dan Robbins, La Paz Intermediate School Music Director, discussed the La Paz Jazz Combo
  and thanked the Council for supporting the arts. He invited the City Council Members and
  residents to a concert at the Murray Community Center on Saturday, May 14, 2016, at 6:00
  p.m.

  The La Paz Combo played My Little Suede Shoes for the Council and audience.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

James F. Farris, M.V.: expressed concern with continued problems at the YMCA and asked to be
placed on the next City Council agenda so the matters can be addressed by the City Council. He
also commented on the rapid deterioration of a home on Destello Street.

Jessica Craig, Wellness Choice, M.V.: announced that Wellness Choice is a family-run business
designed to help keep the community strong by providing services in health, wellness, and weight
loss.

Madelyn Montoya, Families Forward, Irvine: introduced the non-profit which serves south county
families in need with housing sufficiency, a food pantry, and other assistance.

Anrea Santos and Gabby Martinez: announced that they are the co-founders of Rat Park
Foundation which was created to raise awareness about substance abuse and compassion for
people struggling with addiction. They invited the Council Members and audience to a launch
party on Saturday, May 21 from 4:00 to 10:00 p.m. at the Eureka building in Irvine.

Marla Noel, President of Fairhaven Memorial Services, M.V.: thanked the City for the help that
was provided when she was opening a new business in town.

City Council Minutes  2  May 10, 2016
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 5, 7, 8, and 11 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of April 26, 2016, as presented.

4.  Check Register Dated April 22, 2016 in the Amount of $605,666.28

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Requests for a one-time exemption to the “No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption”
  Regulation at City facilities for community events and programs.

  Approved the request for a one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage
  Consumption" Regulation at City facilities.

9.  Cost Allocation Plan and User Fee Study

  Approved the Professional Services Agreement with Willdan Financial Services for the
  preparation of a Cost Allocation Plan and User Fee Study in an amount not to exceed amount
  of $37,715.

10. 2016 Fourth of July Community Street Faire

  Approved the Special Events Permit submitted by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee
  authorizing the annual Mission Viejo Fourth of July Community Street Faire on Monday,
  July 4, 2016.

City Council Minutes  3  May 10, 2016
 12. 2016 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 838)

  Approved the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer,
  and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

13. Bicycle Corridor Improvement Program Grant Application-Arroyo Trabuco Regional
  Multi-Use Trail Access and Regional Connector

  Adopted Resolution 16-18 Authorizing Application for Funds for the Bicycle Corridor
  Improvement Program Funded with Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Improvement
  Program Funding Under the Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century and Fixing
  Americas Surface Transportation Federal Transportation Act for the Arroyo Trabuco
  Regional Multi-Use Trail and Access Regional Connector Project.

14. Website Redesign and Content Management System Implementation

  Approved entering into agreement and issuance of purchase order to Civic Resource Group
  in the amount of $128,244 plus a 10% contingency for consulting services and
  implementation of a new content management system and website redesign.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated April 15, 2016 in the Amount of $730,866.32

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a payment made to the County of Orange for the
  Marguerite pool plan check. She asked what role the County has in the oversight of the
  Marguerite pool project.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay said that the County Health
  Department is required, on behalf of the State of California, to make sure that the pool
  filtration system is adequate and to look at ADA access issues, among other things.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that the title for a storage unit for the Marine
  Adoption Committee was changed to an acronym (MAC). She stated that the public has a
  right to know that the City is expending those funds for the Marine Adoption Committee.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  4  May 10, 2016
  5. Renewal of Rental Permit with Outta Bounds Events for Use of the Thomas R. Potocki
  Conference Center

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report.

  Scott Ramirez, M.V.: asked the Council to renew the Outta Bounds lease of the Potocki
  Center for summer camps and afterschool programs.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to renew
  the rental permit with Outta Bounds Events for use of the Thomas R. Potocki Conference
  Center for 14 months in the amount of $9,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

7.  Amended 2015-2019 Consolidated Plan and Draft Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year
  (FY) 2016-2017 Detailing City’s Proposed Use of Community Development Block
  Grant (CDBG) Funds.

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister and consultant Mike Linares answered
  questions of the City Council.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to adopt
  Resolution 16-16 Approving the City's Amended 2015-2019 Consolidated Plan and Draft
  Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year (FY) 2016-2017 Detailing City's Proposed Use of
  Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds and Authorizing Submission of Such
  Plans to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

8.  OCTA Agency Service Plan for Senior Mobility Program

  Council Member Sachs inquired about the four new delivery areas and whether or not rider
  fees will cover the costs.

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix responded that Measure 2 funds
  will cover the costs.

City Council Minutes  5  May 10, 2016
   Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve OCTA
  Agency Service Plan for Senior Mobility Program and direct staff to look into opportunities
  for for-hire services such as Uber and Lift.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

11.  Annual Review of Residential and Commercial Integrated Waste Management Rates

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she pulled this item from the Consent Calendar
  in order to register a no vote.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to adopt Resolution 16-
  17 Approving the Proposed Trash Rate Adjustments for Residential (1.6% Increase From
  $12.91 to $13.12 per Month), Commercial (1.5% Increase), and Roll-Off (1.4% Increase)
  Services Effective July 1, 2016.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

15. Recommended Names for the Wall of Recognition Display

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve
  the recommended names for the Wall of Recognition Display.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

16. Animal Service Agreements with the Cities of Laguna Hills and Rancho Santa
  Margarita

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  6  May 10, 2016
   Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1)
  approve the Agreements for Animal Control and Shelter Services with the Cities of Laguna
  Hills and Rancho Santa Margarita and authorize the Mayor to sign the agreements for both
  cities; (2) approve the Memorandum of the Understanding (MOU) for Funding the Interior
  Renovation and Expansion of the Mission Viejo Animal Services Administration Building
  and authorize the Mayor to sign the MOU for both cities; (3) adopt Resolution No. 16-19, A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo providing for the revisions to
  Personnel Policies; (4) adopt Resolution No. 16-20, A Resolution of the City Council of the
  City of Mission Viejo amending the City's Authorized Position Schedule for Fiscal Year
  2016-2017; and (5) adopt Resolution No. 16-21, A Resolution of the City Council of the City
  of Mission Viejo amending the City's Salary Schedule and establishing salary ranges for
  authorized job classifications.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

*Items 17 and 18 were taken out of order.

18. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury presented the report.

17. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

19. Moody’s Local Government Issuer Comment Report

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the report.

20. Regulations for Cell Tower Generator Co-location and Co-use

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Mayor Ury, to direct staff to develop
  standards and regulations for back-up generators and co-use of generators for multiple
  carriers.

City Council Minutes  7  May 10, 2016
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

21. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced that Rotary Club will hold its annual fundraiser on June 11,
2016, at the Norman P. Murray Community Center. Registration includes dinner, entertainment
and a Texas Hold 'Em tournament. Tickets are $60 with $50 going to a local charity of the player’s
choice. Council Member Raths informed the community that the Kaleidoscope escalators are up
and running again and he is looking forward to the new hotel at Avery and Marguerite and also a
car wash near that location. He noted that the City is moving forward in support of small
businesses and the Chamber of Commerce, with about 40 small business owners, meets every
Tuesday morning at 8:00 a.m. at High Park tap House and residents are welcome to attend.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs thanked staff for the third monthly aquatics complex update and he
recommended that the summary page is posted on the City’s website so everyone knows where
the project stands. He noted that at the last Council meeting two residents spoke about some break-
ins in their neighborhood and then, over the weekend, he read in the newspaper that nine south
county restaurants were burglarized. Council Member Sachs stated that prisoners are being let out
of jail and some have no place to go. He asked that Lt. NewMyer attend a closed session to report
to the Council on the tactics that the City is using to combat crime because it’s different than it
was a year ago. He recommended that the public also be educated, in open session and/or at the
town hall meeting that Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum plans to hold. Council member Sachs said that
the City prides itself in being a safe city but there seems to be more crime on the streets presently
and he’d like to take a proactive approach and be ready to assuage the residents.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that the Council cannot compromise when it comes to public
safety. She reminded her colleagues of her conclusion that there were eleven Sheriff’s Department
motorcycles which, she said, was based on a March 8, 2016 staff report which stated that the city
maintains a fleet of 11 motorcycles. At that point she didn't realize that the City doesn’t have
City Council Minutes  8  May 10, 2016
 eleven officers for those bikes and she reiterated her position that she believes the City needs more
cruisers on the streets as cruisers deter crime. Council Member Schlicht referenced Vehicle Code
Section 21100 which addresses the regulation of traffic by means of traffic officers. She discussed
a recent traffic signal outage at Marguerite and Crown Valley and noted that it took motorists 30
minutes to get through the intersection. She wondered if the City needs an ordinance that requires
a traffic officer to be present when that type of thing occurs. Council Member Schlicht pointed
out that there are four candidates sitting on the dais. She noted that a recent blog article online
recommended voting for Lisa Bartlett for County Supervisor and Cathy Schlicht for Central
Committee. She also mentioned that California approved the installation of single stall bathrooms
that are open to any gender and she asked how that might affect the City in its expansion of park
restrooms. Council Member Schlicht explained that the bobby hat she had displayed on the dais
was in honor of her mom who was born and raised in Whales and her father, who was a
constable. She informed her colleagues that she voted no on the animal shelter agenda item
because she still believes that the City is increasing the scope and size of government to benefit
citizens outside of the community. In closing, Council Member Schlicht shared a quote from
Clarence S. Darrow: “You can only protect your liberties in this world by protecting the other
man's freedom. You can only be free if I am free.”

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum discussed comments made earlier about the state of the Montanoso
Recreation Center. She said she uses the facility regularly so she doesn’t need to attend a special
field trip to Montanoso. ]She discussed the progress of the bathroom upgrade, a pool filter
malfunction, and the exercise room and stated that things do need repair with high-use recreation
facilities and she wanted to provide an explanation for the public as to why some changes were
made there. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum congratulated staff on a very well done Arts Alive event
and stated that the artwork was terrific and she really enjoyed the Jurassic Park theme. She
discussed her attendance at other recent events including the Elks Club Youth Awards ceremony
the Rotary Club’s National Day of Prayer breakfast, and a SCAG regional conference where she
voted against changing the bylaws on the voting process. She also attended an open house for the
Marguerite Recreation Center, the YMCA and the Aquatics Complex and noted that it was very
well attended and she enjoyed the concert on the court afterwards. She encouraged residents to
attend a regional town hall meeting on sober living homes on May 12, 2016, at 6:00 p.m. at the
Laguna Hills community center. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum outlined other upcoming events
including the Marine Adoption Committee’s Lake Day to honor Marines and their families, Water
Awareness Day, the City’s 1st annual Film Festival, the KSBR Birthday Bash, and the City’s
Memorial Day event at 8:30 a.m. on May 31. She wished the High Park Tap House restaurant a
happy anniversary and encouraged residents to watch for an announcement in the next few weeks
regarding a town hall meeting on the topic of Neighborhood Watch. In closing, Mayor Pro Tem
Bucknum asked Mayor Ury to adjourn the meeting in memory of Betty Boltz.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury thanked everyone associated with the Rotary Prayer breakfast. He said that Master of
Ceremonies Dave Leckness puts his heart and soul into the event and he thanked his colleagues
City Council Minutes  9  May 10, 2016
 for attending. Mayor Ury announced that he does plan to play in the Elks Texas Hold ‘Em
tournament in June and that he was honored to receive an invitation to spend the night on an aircraft
carrier out at sea next week. He said it is going to be a thrill and he will report back to his
colleagues and let them know all about it.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:27 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Betty Boltz, to Tuesday, May 24, 2016, at 5:00
p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 24, 2016

City Council Minutes  10  May 10, 2016
